subject: Pricing & Batching: continuous batching expectations and unit economics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>, Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing & Batching: continuous batching expectations and unit economics

Hi Alex / Jane -

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and a few follow-ups so we can prepare a tailored pricing estimate and technical recommendation:

1) Token volumes: please confirm expected monthly token range (min / typical / peak). In our call you mentioned pilot ~50M/mo with potential scale to 200M+/mo - please confirm.
2) Budget & unit economics: what is your target $/1M tokens (ballpark) for production? This helps us recommend model variants and batching strategies.
3) Workload patterns: you described a steady stream of small user queries with occasional batch jobs overnight. Can you confirm expected concurrency (avg and peak) and typical sequence lengths (avg tokens in + out)?
4) Continuous batching expectations: are you expecting a continuously open traffic profile where continuous batching should be leveraged, or are workloads more spiky with short burst windows?

Attached: token-estimates.xlsx (please review / correct). We'll also include a preliminary cost sheet and recommended batch/concurrency knobs after we get your numbers.

Next steps: if you can reply with the items above, Camila (SE) and I will produce: a) a 3-tier pricing table (1M/10M/100M token buckets), b) recommended batching and concurrency settings, and c) expected unit economics for both hosted and Dedicated options.

Thanks - talk soon.

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & Batching: continuous batching expectations and unit economics

Thanks for the recap, Aditya - good call. Quick answers below and I've attached a more detailed traffic extract (token-estimates.xlsx).

1) Monthly token volumes: pilot month ~50M tokens, Q3 target 150M, long-term steady state 300M-400M/mo if conversion hits. Peak day could be ~20% above daily average.
2) Budget / target unit economics: for production we need to be around $200-$350 per 1M tokens (internal goal). If we can get under $200 that's ideal.
3) Workload patterns: mostly continuous user-facing queries across US timezones. Average concurrency ~8-12, peak concurrency ~30 during promo spikes. Typical request size is small: 30 tokens in, 40 tokens out average (so ~70 tokens per request). We also have nightly batch jobs (~5% of traffic) that run larger requests (avg 1k tokens).
4) Continuous batching: yes - traffic is fairly constant (not extreme spikes every hour) so continuous batching makes sense. We care about tail latency for user queries; batching should not add more than ~50-80ms p50 on top of baseline.

Procurement: copying Jane for contract/budgetary questions.

Appreciate next steps and the pricing table.

Best,
Alex
Head of Product | Acme Retail

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & Batching: continuous batching expectations and unit economics

Alex - thanks for the detail, very helpful. A few technical notes from SE side to align expectations:

- Given ~70 tokens/request and concurrency ~8-12, continuous batching should deliver significant cost savings with minimal latency impact if we use small batch windows (20-50ms) and set a max batch size around 16-32 depending on GPU profile.
- For your nightly 1k-token batch jobs, we'll route those to a separate worker pool to avoid blocking low-latency traffic; batching on long sequences gives good throughput improvement.
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for common conversation prefixes (reduces repeated compute on system prompts) - this can cut token compute by ~5-15% depending on hit rate.
- Ballpark unit economics (very approximate until we size model variant): with continuous batching and a 16-32 batch size on an Llama-2-class open model, expect $120-$250 per 1M tokens at scale; for higher-quality paid models add a delta. We'll prepare a more precise breakdown in the pricing table.

Sharing internal runbook on batching best practices: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batching-best-practices
Also attaching our pricing sheet.

I'll draft two config proposals: (A) low-latency optimized (p50 latency target + small batch windows) and (B) throughput-optimized (larger batches, slightly higher p50) and include expected $/1M for each.

-Camila
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-retail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & Batching: continuous batching expectations and unit economics

Thanks Aditya / Camila - that all sounds reasonable. Next steps for us:

- Please send a preliminary pricing table for 1M / 10M / 100M token buckets for both hosted and Dedicated options, with the two config proposals you mentioned (low-latency vs throughput).
- Include expected p50/p95 latency impact for the low-latency config and an estimated $/1M token line for each bucket.
- We'll review with procurement - Jane, can you confirm preferred cadence for an internal review?

Can we target early next week for the pricing deck and a demo of the Dedicated route (if possible)?

Appreciate it,
Alex
